attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post, given in his voice in a list of points against OpenAI. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The draft says public skepticism about OpenAI and Altman is rising. That matches 'people are becoming more skeptical about the company and its CEO'. It is an unhedged present-tense observation about a trend up to the post date.

contract.note: Marcus named no measure, population or baseline. The plain reading is a recent rise in doubt about both OpenAI and Altman by Aug 9, 2025, with no majority required and launch-related rises allowed. That is an ordinary, fair reading. Requiring both targets follows from his wording.

evidence.note: Ars Technica, Aug 11, 2025, reports a flood of user complaints after the GPT-5 launch by Aug 8. It shows anger about the product and the rollout. It does not measure a change in trust in OpenAI or Altman.

A qualitative arXiv study (v4, Mar 2026, before the evaluation date) of 150 posts from Aug 8–9, 2025. It covers attachment and resistance to the model switch. It has no before-and-after trust measure and no separate measure for OpenAI or Altman.

reviews.rationale: Both evidence items show a backlash against the GPT-5 launch. Neither is comparable or systematic evidence that skepticism rose toward both OpenAI and Altman by Aug 9, 2025. The contract says product dissatisfaction and selected complaints are not enough. The packet has no surveys or sentiment trends, and nothing shows skepticism was stable or falling. The evidence settles the claim neither way.
